package_info.package_name: Popup Builder WordPress plugin (malicious Custom JS injection)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all vulnerable versions with stored XSS flaw)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers exploit a stored XSS vulnerability in the Popup Builder plugin to inject malicious JavaScript into the Custom JS or CSS sections, resulting in unauthorized redirections and malware delivery to site visitors.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits an infected site page)
execution_context.file_location: Popup Builder plugin's Custom JS section (stored in WordPress database, rendered in page HTML)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes in the browser of any visitor to an infected page, reads the user's cookies, and redirects the browser to a malicious domain with the cookie data appended as a URL parameter, enabling credential/session theft and further malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code exfiltrates sensitive user data (cookies) and forcibly redirects users to an external, attacker-controlled domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Custom JS in WordPress plugins is expected to enhance site functionality, not to steal user data or perform unauthorized redirections.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate redirection scripts may be used for login flows or A/B testing, but never with exfiltration of cookies or to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Use of <script> tag in Custom JS section

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits an infected site page)
execution_context.file_location: Popup Builder plugin's Custom JS section (stored in WordPress database, rendered in page HTML)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code loads and executes a remote JavaScript payload from an attacker-controlled server, enabling arbitrary code execution in the context of the victim's browser, which can lead to further malware injection, credential theft, or drive-by downloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and executing remote scripts from untrusted domains is a classic method for delivering malware and taking control of user sessions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Custom JS should not load code from external, untrusted sources, especially without user consent or validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate sites may load scripts from trusted CDNs, but not from unknown or suspicious domains.
key_indicators: External script source from non-whitelisted domain

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits stored XSS vulnerability in Popup Builder plugin to inject malicious JavaScript into the Custom JS section.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is stored in the WordPress database and rendered on site pages.

attack_chain.action: When a user visits an infected page, the malicious JavaScript executes in their browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected to attacker-controlled domain and/or additional malware is loaded.

attack_chain.action: Malicious domain receives exfiltrated data (e.g., cookies) or delivers further payloads to the victim.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential/session theft, further compromise, or malware infection.

behavioral_signatures: Custom JS or CSS in WordPress plugins containing <script> tags with document.cookie access
Custom JS loading external scripts from non-whitelisted domains
Unexpected client-side redirections to external domains
file_indicators: Popup Builder plugin's Custom JS or CSS fields containing suspicious JavaScript
Presence of <script>window.location=... or <script src=... in plugin configuration
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to unknown or suspicious domains from site visitors' browsers
Redirections to domains not associated with the legitimate site
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the Custom JS and CSS fields of the Popup Builder plugin for suspicious script tags, especially those accessing document.cookie or loading external scripts. Analyze web traffic for unexpected redirections or requests to untrusted domains. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to block or alert on script injections and outbound connections to known malicious domains.
